Bitcoin may be pumping this morning... but the crowd remains fearful and bored.

I looked at 19 periods of time when people were as checked out as they are today and investigated the average returns afterward.

The results are quite bullish. https://t.co/UItsRFWjGY

I get why Bitcoiners are so fearful right now.

This sell-off has been brutal, but one thing that has stood out to me is how bored people have been during this downward price action.

In many ways, fear and boredom are conflicting emotions.

Fear inspires action and focus.

Boredom is more about a lack of interest.

When both happen at the same time, it indicates a unique psychological event. Because of this, it’s interesting to look back through Bitcoin’s history and look at other periods of time where a similar collection of emotions was firing

One of the primary ones that I keep coming back to is in early 2020.

Today we will:

1) Look at some historical mood data from 2020 and why it is similar to today.

2) Calculate how Bitcoin normally performs after boring periods just like this one.

I know there’s a lot of negativity and doom out on the timeline. But it’s precisely during periods like this that I think it’s important to remind ourselves why we remain bullish on this asset, and how positively the orange coin has typically performed after periods like the one we are experiencing right now.

Let’s dive in.

BREAKING: Jensen Huang releases a statement after being reinstated as CEO of Nvidia, $NVDA:

Full statement:

"I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution. I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process. I am especially grateful to Harvey Jones for his leadership as Chair, and to Colette Kress and our executive staff for leading NVIDIA during this period. I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can’t wait to get back to work."

Jensen has been reinstated as CEO with immediate effect.

Bitcoin is in a much different place now than it was in early 2020. But from a crowd psychology perspective, the current sell-off has surprising similarities.

The high levels of fear both then and now are to be expected. But in both cases, Bitcoiners became extremely bored.

Bitcoiners who survived the brutal COVID sell-off enjoyed ~10x return over the next year.

It's impossible to know what will happen in the short term, but historically, when the crowd is as bored and defeated as it is right now, it's marked fantastic buying opportunities.

Good luck.
